title: giana sisters: twisted dreams
text: Let's start with the good things about this game: It's pretty (although it's not Trine), it's difficult in a challenging way, the repetitive music isn't irritating, some of the bits of levels are really well designed and make you feel great when getting through them and the twisting/changing world mechanic is well used. The bad? Everything else. The first two bosses are easy, the last one too hard (over an hour to beat ffs). Too many parts of the games' levels are badly made and rely on knowing what's coming next; there's just no way of seeing what's going to kill you just off screen until you hit it. The levels themselves are very samey and generally forgettable. Dying doesn't feel like a new opportunity but rather a frustration and a test in patience. That thing that looks like a platform? It's not. That platform that you can jump on? It's slightly transparent in this world and you'll fall through it. Those purple spikes against a purple background? You'll see them when you walk into them...Lastly, you need a certain about of stars to unlock a boss. For a lot of people that will mean back tracking through levels and replaying them soley for the sake of getting those last few stars. Great way to elongate a game and a great way to annoy people that just want to do the next bit. There are other modes including time trial and I can go over levels again and again trying to get more stars but I'm just fed up with it and have no desire to ever go back to this. It's a shame, I like difficult games. VVVVVV and Super Meat Boy frustrated me but I'll always love them. This is just going into the virtual bin along with an empty box of headache pills.

text: I wanted to like this game.  The graphical style is nice, the dual world mechanic with 2 playable characters you can switch out at any time is a good feature but the gameplay is just dull. My biggest frustration with it by far is that the levels are too long.  They are not interesting enough to play through and the 2 types of enemies I encountered in the first 6 levels are brainless jump pads.  To fill out the unnecessarily large levels you have hundreds of gems to collect, they are everywhere and as I’m not someone that enjoys heavy lashings of collectibles in games this just added to the tedium. Add in a poor checkpoint system and I gave up by the end of the first world (6 levels in).  Not because I found it too hard, I just found it boring. Half the level size, shrink the collectibles down to a handful (or keep the hundreds of gems but add something else more meaningful to collect in much smaller numbers) and give the enemies more character (from my experience of the first world that I played). That in my opinion would give you a tighter, more enjoyable experience. For reference I would say Super Mario World is the best 2D platformer ever made.  Meatboy and the rayman Origins are right up there too.  I bring this up because as much as I loved Rayman Legends, the games “more is better” style with the lums was very off putting to me.  If it didn’t bother you there it probably won’t bother you here.

title: giana sisters: twisted dreams
text: Fifteen levels in and I feel I can safely recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of the platforming genre.  The core gameplay combines facets of three of my favorite platformers: helicopter slowfalls a la Donkey Kong Country 2/3, Sonic the Hedgehog's homing attack, and the dimension/color changing in Outland.  Giana Sisters does enough on its own and offers some relatively unique level experiences, but all in all it seems more like a tribute to the games I have previously mentioned.  For the completionist or competitor there is much to do after the main game; there is score/time attack as well as higher difficulty modes (simply no checkpoints or 1 life runs of the entire game). If you are looking for a 2D platformer on Steam I have run into very few that were better than Giana Sisters.

title: giana sisters: twisted dreams
text: Being a kid of the 1980s, I truely love this game! It might only have the name in common with the original Giana Sisters from back then, but still it totally FEELS 1980sh!  3D wasn't really a topic back then, we were happy about 16-color games with simple but catchy chip music, scrolling (hopefully smoothly) in 2 directions... if you asked me in '85 what I'd imagine games to be like in the far far future, my answer woulda been something like Giana Sisters Twisted Dreams. With oooh so many colors, scrolling perfectly smoothly in ALL directions in multiple layers (parallax!) and of course Chris Hülsbeck music... here we go! Yes, for todays standards the game is hard. Hard but fair, on "normal" difficulty it's doable if you ain't got no overly clumsy fingers. Only the boss monsters are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥but with some patience even those can be cracked. We are a bit spoiled nowadays... I mean, in the original Giana Sisters you had like... what was it... three lives? And that was it... three mistakes and game over, and return to the very beginning! Today, on "normal" you got unlimited lives here, you'll only get kicled back to the last of many check points. And except for the painintheassified bosses, I love everything about that game. The colorful graphics, the perfect jump'n run feeling, the driving sound track, the morphable backgrounds, drat, even gem hunting can be so frickin' motivating! The game is full of awesome ideas and in my opinion it's one of the damn best platformers of all times for the PC! Warmly recommended!
